Paper: Are Watermarked Images Editable? SafeMark for Watermark-Preserving Text-Guided Image Editing (Wu et al.)
Problem: Make diffusion editors preserve a pre-existing watermark
Attack/editing setting: Text-guided semantic editing of watermarked real and generated images; plus post-edit distortions
Metrics: Bit accuracy; FID, IS, CLIP similarity
Dataset: LSUN-Church, LSUN-Bedroom, CelebA, AFHQ-Dog (100 imgs each) + generated counterparts
Method: Fine-tunes the editor with a thresholded watermark-decoding loss added to the editing objective
Main result: Bit acc ~1.0 vs 0.3-0.6 for unprotected editors at comparable FID/CLIP (per paper)
Limitation: Requires editor fine-tuning per editor and differentiable editor; older domain-specific editors; no sequential editing; no instruction editors
Code availability (URL + license if know: No public code found (paper mentions PyTorch implementation only)
Relation to our work: Closest prior for watermark-preserving editing (training-based). Our training-free / instruction-editor / sequential angle is not covered

Paper: Guidance Watermarking for Diffusion Models (Gesny, Giboulot, Furon, Chappelier)
Problem: Embed watermark during generation without retraining
Attack/editing setting: Generation; robustness to standard transforms via augmentation in guidance
Method: Training-free guidance of diffusion sampling with gradients of a post-hoc watermark decoder (with augmentations)
Main result: Converts post-hoc schemes into in-generation schemes; little change to image for given seed/prompt
Limitation: Generation only, not editing of an already-watermarked image; not sequential
Relation to our work: Most directly transferable technique: decoder-gradient guidance inside an editor's sampling loop = training-free watermark-aware editing

Paper: Editing Away the Evidence: Diffusion-Based Image Manipulation and the Failure Modes of Robust Watermarking (Qi, Tang, Lee, Davis, Carter)
Problem: Analyze why diffusion editing destroys watermarks
Editing model: InstructPix2Pix, UltraEdit-trained, DragDiffusion, InstantDrag, DragFlow, TF-ICON, SHINE
Attack/editing setting: Diffusion editing at varying strength t*
Metrics: Bit acc, BER, AUC, FPR@TPR, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS, CLIP/DINOv2
Main result: Bit acc 71-85% at t*=0.4; 53-61% at t*=0.8 (per paper)
Limitation: Part of a cluster of near-templated papers sharing co-authors 'Emily Davis', 'Finn Carter' (see 2510.05978, 2511.05598, 2603.04696, 2603.29736); credibility should be treated cautiously; no code

Paper: Diffusion-Based Image Editing for Breaking Robust Watermarks (Ni, Carter, Niu, Davis, Zhang)
Problem: Watermark removal via diffusion regeneration and decoder-guided attack
Method: Regeneration + guided diffusion using decoder gradients to erase
Limitation: Same templated author cluster; no code
Relation to our work: Shows decoder-guided sampling works for removal; mirror image of our preservation guidance

Paper: Diffusion-Based Image Editing: An Unforeseen Adversary to Robust Invisible Watermarks (Fu, Carter, Wang, Davis, Zhang)
When Denoising Becomes Unsigning (Gu, Tang, Wen, Davis, Carter); also 2511.10933 (Ni et al.), 2602.20680 (Guo et al.), 2603.29736 (Hu et al.)
Problem: Information-theoretic fragility of watermarks under diffusion editing
Main result: MI -> 0 as edit strength grows (per abstracts)

Paper: A Somewhat Robust Image Watermark against Diffusion-based Editing Models (RIW; Tan et al.)
Watermark: RIW: per-image PGD-optimized invisible watermark in SD latent space
Method: Adversarial per-image optimization using SD encoder/decoder (no exact editor access)
Main result: ~96% extraction after InstructPix2Pix vs 0% for conventional (per paper)
Limitation: ~95 s/image embedding; single edit only; text-pattern watermark
Code availability (URL + license if know: Anonymous repo mentioned in paper (UNVERIFIED URL)
Relation to our work: Robust-embedding baseline (embed side), not editor side

Paper: Robust-Wide: Robust Watermarking against Instruction-driven Image Editing (Hu et al.)
Problem: Train watermark encoder/decoder robust to instruction editing
Watermark: Robust-Wide (64-bit, encoder-decoder, post-hoc on any image)
Editing model: InstructPix2Pix (training), ControlNet-IP2P, MagicBrush, inpainting, DDIM inversion
Single or sequential: Single + continual editing up to 3 rounds (InstructPix2Pix, 30 real images, figure only)
Method: PIDSG: gradients through last k editor sampling steps during watermark training
Main result: BER ~2.6% for 64 bits after editing; extractable after 3 rounds (qualitative per-round curve)
Limitation: Embedding-side; sequential test tiny (30 imgs) and not systematic; trained against one editor
Relation to our work: Closest prior evidence on sequential editing + watermark; our work must go beyond 3 rounds/30 imgs and treat editor side

Paper: Robust Watermarking Using Generative Priors Against Image Editing: From Benchmarking to Advances (VINE / W-Bench; Lu et al.)
Watermark: VINE-B, VINE-R (SDXL-Turbo based) + 11 baselines (MBRS, CIN, PIMoG, RivaGAN, SepMark, TrustMark, DWTDCT, DWTDCTSVD, SSL, StegaStamp, EditGuard)
Editing model: InstructPix2Pix, MagicBrush, UltraEdit, ControlNet-Inpainting, SVD (I2V), stochastic/deterministic regeneration
Attack/editing setting: Regeneration, global editing, local editing (mask sizes), I2V
Metrics: TPR@0.1%FPR, bit acc, AUROC, PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, FID
Method: Watermark encoder built on generative prior, trained with blur surrogate attacks; VINE-R fine-tuned with IP2P
Main result: VINE best overall robustness on W-Bench
Code availability (URL + license if know: https://github.com/Shilin-LU/VINE (NTU NTUITIVE non-commercial license); W-Bench on HuggingFace Shilin-LU/W-Bench
Relation to our work: Primary benchmark to reuse; we extend W-Bench to sequential edits and editor-side intervention
